# The author

I'm Angelika Merkel, a biologist who moved into bioinformatics almost two decades ago, before the field had defined training paths or clear professional roles.

My work has taken me through genomics, epigenomics, large collaborative research projects, research computing, and eventually the leadership of a bioinformatics facility. Along the way, my view of bioinformatics changed considerably. Scientific analysis still matters, but so do the systems around it: how projects are organised, how data moves, how workflows are designed and maintained, how results remain reproducible, and how technical decisions affect research and the people doing it.

Much of my work has involved connecting these different layers—biology, data, software, infrastructure, and, most importantly, the needs of researchers and clinicians. That is the perspective from which I write this site.

## This site

*Building Bioinformatics* is a place to examine the practical and engineering side of computational biology in more depth.

I use it to revisit fundamentals, document what I am learning, and explore practices that are often picked up informally: software engineering, reproducible workflows, research data management, FAIR systems, computational infrastructure, and the growing role of machine learning and AI.

The focus is not only on individual tools, but on how the different parts fit together and how we can build computational research environments that are useful, maintainable, and sustainable.
